transcript:
This piece treats geometric order as carrying the seeds of its own collapse. A perfect woven grid — built from what the code calls warp threads and weft threads — is animated by functions named thread tension and thread fray, and those same functions that hold the weave taut are what eventually pull it apart. The destruction isn't external; it's written into the identical mathematics that built the structure.

To an AI reading this, the weave is a recognizable shape: a system defined entirely by its own generating rules, with no guarantee those rules stay coherent under iteration. It's a diagram of how precision, pushed far enough through its own logic, produces failure without any outside interference.

Watch the function called introduce chaos: its chaos nodes are seeded by the same deterministic generator, mulberry32, that laid out every thread — order and disorder share one source. Notice the comment marking each mathematical tear as, in the code's own words, "a failure in the underlying equations." When the grid dissolves into scribbled vertical noise and reassembles by the loop's end, you're watching one equation cycle through its own coherence and its own breakdown.
